_doc: Hook-parity ledger (T01). One row per legacy .claude/hooks/*.sh script. `core` is the single shared owner of the algorithm (hooks/core/*.mjs, run through scripts/hook-runner.mjs); `hosts.<host>` records the native event, the response the host actually supports and the honest state: `ported` (shared core + adapter + tests), `conditional` (only when a precondition holds), `legacy-only` (still served by the Bash script under .claude/hooks only), `project-owned` (never packaged), `retired` (needs rationale + decision). `activation` is `none` until an installed-host run (T16) proves the behavior; unit tests never flip it. Validated by scripts/lib/parity.mjs; rendered to docs/harness/hook-parity.md.
activation_note: No real project has activated the ported hooks. Legacy .claude/hooks/*.sh stay registered in .claude/settings.json until an installed-host run records their replacement (installation.md → Activation). A unit test is not an activation.

hooks.behavior: Refuse `git commit` when the staged set of the target repository is empty; resolve the repo from `git -C`, a leading `cd`, then the caller cwd; audit the staged set.
known_limits: Chained `git add X && git commit` is blocked by design (the index is inspected before the chain runs).
Only `git -C <dir>` and a leading `cd <dir> &&` are parsed; other directory changes fall back to the caller cwd.

hooks.behavior: Scan the per-commit patches about to be published for known-format secrets, private keys, credential connection strings, hardcoded credential assignments and credential filenames; block with paths only; explicit audited override.
known_limits: Allowlisted paths (examples, lockfiles, docs, fixtures, this guard) are not scanned — a secret placed in a `.md` file ships.
Without git the check cannot run: it reports the missing infrastructure and does not claim protection.

hooks.behavior: First code edit per memory domain per author context is blocked until a scoped memory preparation marker exists; dormant until domain rules exist and memory exceeds the size threshold.

codex.context: session_id only — subagents share the parent id; a child cannot be told apart, so the guard requires an explicit per-executor preflight receipt or blocks the capability

known_limits: The marker is an acknowledgement, not proof the model understood memory.

hooks.behavior: Comment-noise nudge above configured density; tests, stories, generated and vendored files exempt; never blocks.
First matching project-configured file-class reminder; same exclusions as guard-comments; never blocks.
Reroute advice for misplaced errors.md entries; active only with app_source_regex; never deletes or moves.
Local read telemetry per memory file into a gitignored sidecar; archive excluded; writes not counted as reads; malformed sidecar self-heals.

codex.note: Codex has no Read tool event; only shell reads are observed. Missing telemetry is unknown usage, never evidence a file is unused.

known_limits: Best-effort counter; a lost increment under concurrent hooks is acceptable.

hooks.behavior: Local best-effort audit line per tool call with bounded retention; never a gate.

codex.note: Hosted web tools carry no hook; fetches are not audited on Codex.

known_limits: Attempted (PreToolUse) and completed (PostToolUse) events are distinct lines; prompts, contents and credentials are never logged.

hooks.behavior: Symbol-shaped Grep gets a pointer to LSP navigation; only meaningful with a declared LSP.

claude.precondition: project declares an LSP (rules Code Navigation section present)

codex.note: Codex has no structured Grep tool and no symbol-navigation surface; parsing shell bodies as if they were Grep is not a port.

hooks.behavior: Warn once when the hook runtime dependencies are missing; silent when healthy; never blocks.
known_limits: Missing infrastructure is reported as missing protection, never as healthy enforcement.

hooks.behavior: Project-owned toolchain / MCP / credential-presence check; never packaged; both hosts delegate to the project's exact script with the project root as cwd.
known_limits: Its .env presence checks stay inside the script; the runner never reads .env and never exports its output to a reviewer.
